HTML Entity Encoder

Escape text into HTML entities and decode entities back to text, both directions done correctly.

Encoding escapes & < > " ' and maps common Latin-1 characters to named entities. Decoding uses the browser's HTML parser, so every entity type is handled.

📖 How to use

  1. Choose Encode or Decode at the top.
  2. Type or paste your text — conversion happens live.
  3. Switch modes any time; the text converts in place.
  4. Copy the result with one click.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What exactly does encoding change?

Encode escapes &, <, >, " and ' and converts common Latin-1 characters (like é and ©) to named entities. Decoding reverses all of it.

Does decoding handle numeric entities like &#233;?

Yes. Decoding uses the browser's own HTML parser, so every named, decimal and hexadecimal entity is handled.

Is double-encoded text decoded one level at a time?

Yes — decoding “&amp;lt;” gives “&lt;”, not “<”. Each pass decodes exactly one level.
